text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Friday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- On Christmas Eve four alleged extortionists were shot dead and another four injured by a shop keeper in Panevezys. He refused to pay his protection money and fired 26 shots after being attacked.
- The election campaign of the five parliamentary parties cost them nearly three million litas. The winning Homeland Union has spent more than a million.
- Litimpeks bank registered a new share issue worth 15 million litas last week and boosted its share capital to 56.1 million litas from 41.1 million.
- Seventy kidney transplant operations were carried out in Vilnius this year but 250 patients remain on the waiting list.

- Dissatisfied with promises made by the government to raise salaries in a year, the medical profession in Lithuania has now threatened a general strike if their salaries do not reach the average public sector level before the year end.
- The new session of Lithuanian parliament is scheduled for January 9.

- The Homeland Union (Conservative) party will pay back the loan taken on the name of the finance minister Rolandas Matiliauskas from the bancrupt Kredito bank if the real creditor stops paying the debt, Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius told the press. One of the biggest share holders of Kredito bank, Genadijus Rapoportov had asked Matiliauskas to take two loans on his name, both worth $18,000 in 1993 and July 1995 respectively. Half of the credit has been paid back by Rapoportov so far.
